After reviewing the weaknesses:

W1 (Total vs segment revenue): CHALLENGE_REFUTED. E3 explicitly refers to "total revenue" of $64.71 billion (constant currency) for Q3 2026, confirming that the 26% growth figure in E5 refers to total revenue, not just a segment.

W2 (FX effects): CHALLENGE_REFUTED. While E3 confirms FX had an unfavorable impact, the actual reported revenue still grew 26% year-over-year. The claim is about reported revenue growth (not constant currency), and the 26% reported growth clearly exceeds the 20% threshold. The FX headwind of $113 million is immaterial relative to the $13.39 billion absolute increase.

W3 (One-time items): NO_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE. The evidence shows revenue growth was driven by normal business operations (advertising, WhatsApp, subscriptions). While a one-time expense is mentioned, no one-time revenue items are disclosed that would distort the comparison.

The initial SUPPORTED verdict remains correct. Meta's Q3 2026 revenue increased 26% year-over-year, which exceeds the claim's threshold of "more than 20%."
